1991. India is almost broke... There's foreign money left for only a few weeks of imports.
1991. India దాదాపు దివాలా అంచున ఉంది... కొన్ని వారాల imports కి సరిపడా foreign money మాత్రమే మిగిలింది.
So the government quietly sends nearly 47 tonnes of India's gold abroad... as security for a loan.
It worked. India got the money, and survived.
Now jump to 2024... India starts doing the exact opposite.
Over 100 tonnes, flown back from London... Then 102 more, right before Diwali.
In 2023, only 38 percent of RBI's gold was in India... By March 2026? About 77.
So why bring it home?
In 2022, Western countries froze about 300 billion dollars of Russia's reserves... sitting in other countries' vaults.
A lot of countries took one lesson from that... keep your gold where you can reach it.
In 1991, India's gold left to save the country... Now it's coming home to protect it.

అప్పుడు government రహస్యంగా దాదాపు నలభై ఏడు టన్నుల gold ని విదేశాలకు పంపింది... ఒక loan కి హామీగా.
అది పనిచేసింది. India గట్టెక్కింది.
ఇప్పుడు 2024 కి వద్దాం... India సరిగ్గా రివర్స్ చేయడం మొదలుపెట్టింది.
London నుంచి వంద టన్నులకు పైగా gold తిరిగి వచ్చింది... దీపావళికి ముందు ఇంకో నూట రెండు టన్నులు.
2023 లో RBI gold లో ముప్పై ఎనిమిది శాతం మాత్రమే India లో ఉండేది... March 2026 కి? దాదాపు డెబ్బై ఏడు.
మరి ఎందుకు ఇంటికి తెస్తున్నారు?
2022 లో Western countries, వేరే దేశాల vaults లో ఉన్న Russia కి చెందిన దాదాపు మూడు వందల billion dollars ని ఫ్రీజ్ చేశాయి.
దాంతో చాలా దేశాలు ఒక పాఠం నేర్చుకున్నాయి... మీ gold మీకు అందే చోటే ఉంచుకోండి.
1991 లో దేశాన్ని కాపాడటానికి gold బయటికి వెళ్ళింది... ఇప్పుడు దేశాన్ని రక్షించడానికి తిరిగి వస్తోంది.
Indian homes are sitting on about 25,000 tonnes of gold.
Now add up the top 10 central banks in the world. America, Germany, Italy, France, Russia, China, Switzerland, even our own RBI, Japan, the Netherlands... Indian homes still have more.
So why do Indians trust gold more than a bank? It's not just tradition. It's math.
Say you put 10,000 rupees into gold in 2006. Today, it's worth about 1.77 lakh. Nearly 18 times.
The same 10,000 in a bank FD, even at a steady 7 percent a year? About 38,000.
Here's the hidden reason. Gold has one price for the whole world. The rupee doesn't. In 2006, one dollar cost about 45 rupees. Today, about 95.
So when the rupee loses value... your gold doesn't. It quietly protects your savings.
And when you need cash fast? Pledge your gold, and the loan comes in minutes, with very little paperwork.
That's why gold loans are now India's second-biggest kind of retail loan, after home loans. About 16 lakh crore rupees.
So the next time your mom, your sister, or your girlfriend buys gold... they're not wasting money.
They're saving it. For the future.
మన ఇళ్ళల్లో దాదాపు ఇరవై ఐదు వేల టన్నుల gold ఉంది.
ఇప్పుడు ప్రపంచంలోని టాప్ పది central banks ని కలపండి. America, Germany, Italy, France, Russia, China, Switzerland, మన RBI కూడా, Japan, Netherlands... అయినా మన ఇళ్ళల్లోనే ఎక్కువ ఉంది.
మరి Indians కి bank కంటే gold మీదే ఎందుకు ఇంత నమ్మకం? ఇది సంప్రదాయం మాత్రమే కాదు. ఇది లెక్క.
2006 లో మీరు పది వేల రూపాయల gold కొన్నారనుకోండి. ఇప్పుడు దాని విలువ దాదాపు ఒక లక్ష డెబ్బై ఏడు వేలు. దాదాపు పద్దెనిమిది రెట్లు.
అదే పది వేలు bank FD లో, ఏడాదికి ఏడు శాతం చొప్పున పెరిగినా? దాదాపు ముప్పై ఎనిమిది వేలు మాత్రమే.
అసలు రహస్యం ఇది. Gold కి ప్రపంచమంతా ఒకటే ధర. Rupee కి అలా కాదు. 2006 లో ఒక dollar దాదాపు నలభై ఐదు రూపాయలు. ఇప్పుడు దాదాపు తొంభై ఐదు.
అంటే rupee విలువ తగ్గినా... మీ gold విలువ తగ్గదు. మీ savings ని నిశ్శబ్దంగా కాపాడుతుంది.
డబ్బు అర్జెంటుగా కావాలా? Gold తాకట్టు పెడితే, కొన్ని నిమిషాల్లో loan వస్తుంది, పెద్దగా paperwork లేకుండా.
అందుకే ఇప్పుడు India లో home loans తర్వాత రెండో అతిపెద్ద retail loan, gold loan. దాదాపు పదహారు లక్షల కోట్ల రూపాయలు.
అందుకే మీ అమ్మ, మీ చెల్లి, లేదా మీ girlfriend gold కొంటే... వాళ్ళు డబ్బు వృథా చేయట్లేదు.
భవిష్యత్తు కోసం దాచుకుంటున్నారు.
In January, gold hit about $5,590 an ounce. This week? It slipped below $4,000.
That's almost 30 percent gone in nine months. So what happened to the "safest" thing you can own?
Reason one. Gold doesn't pay you anything. A bank FD pays interest. Gold just… sits there.
So when interest rates go up, gold looks less attractive. And in September, America's Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023.
Reason two. Oil jumped on US-Iran tension. Oil up means prices up… and even more fear of rate hikes.
Reason three. When stock markets fall, big investors need cash, fast. And the easiest thing to sell? Gold.
The fast money that rushed in back in January… is now rushing out.
But here's what nobody's talking about. In September, central banks bought about 63 tonnes of gold. The most in almost two years.
So the traders are selling… and the central banks are buying.
And this isn't new. In 2011, gold set a record. It took nine years to beat it, in 2020.
Still, since 2006, it's up about 17 times in rupees.
Gold goes up and down like everything else. That's why people who hold it… think in years, not weeks.

But gold still has a few secrets. Why is an Olympic gold medal… mostly silver? Andhra Pradesh just opened a new gold mine. So why does India still buy almost all its gold from abroad? మొదటి కారణం. Gold మనకి ఏమీ interest ఇవ్వదు. Bank FD interest ఇస్తుంది. Gold అలా ఉంటుంది అంతే.
అందుకే interest rates పెరిగితే, gold మీద ఆసక్తి తగ్గుతుంది. September లో America Fed, 2023 తర్వాత మొదటిసారి rates పెంచింది.
రెండో కారణం. America-Iran tension వల్ల oil ధర పెరిగింది. Oil పెరిగితే అన్ని ధరలు పెరుగుతాయి… rates ఇంకా పెంచుతారేమో అనే భయం.
మూడో కారణం. Stock markets పడినప్పుడు, పెద్ద investors కి అర్జెంటుగా cash కావాలి. అమ్మడానికి అన్నిటికంటే easy? Gold.
January లో వేగంగా వచ్చిన డబ్బు… ఇప్పుడు అంతే వేగంగా బయటికి వెళ్తోంది.
కానీ ఎవరూ మాట్లాడని విషయం ఇది. September లో central banks దాదాపు 63 టన్నుల gold కొన్నాయి. దాదాపు రెండేళ్లలో ఇదే ఎక్కువ.
అంటే traders అమ్ముతున్నారు… central banks కొంటున్నాయి.
ఇది కొత్తేమీ కాదు. 2011 లో gold record కొట్టింది. ఆ record దాటడానికి తొమ్మిదేళ్లు పట్టింది, 2020 వరకు.
అయినా 2006 నుంచి చూస్తే, rupees లో ఇప్పటికీ దాదాపు 17 రెట్లు పెరిగింది.
Gold కూడా అన్నిటిలాగే పెరుగుతుంది, పడుతుంది. అందుకే gold ఉంచుకునేవాళ్ళు… వారాల్లో కాదు, సంవత్సరాల్లో ఆలోచిస్తారు.

Anna! Anna! I have so many Diwali questions!
speaker: CHELLI

text: Okay… what happened?
speaker: ANNA

text: Why does Diwali come on a different date every year? Why does everyone clean the whole house before Diwali? Is my Diwali bonus a gift, or do they have to pay it? Is that photo of India glowing from space real? Why does the stock market open on Diwali? And why can't Delhi breathe after Diwali? Oh, and why does Nepal worship dogs on Diwali? Why did New York give schools a Diwali holiday? And why do green crackers still pollute?
speaker: CHELLI

text: Slow down, slow down! … One at a time.
speaker: ANNA

text: Let's take them one by one… and find the answers.
speaker: ANNA

text: Actually, wait. … Let me record this. If you have these questions, so do a lot of people. I'll put it on YouTube, so anyone who's wondering can learn too.
speaker: ANNA

text: Hi everyone!
speaker: CHELLI

text: So. … What was the first one?
speaker: ANNA

text: Why does Diwali keep jumping around? Last year it was October 20th. This year, November 8th.
speaker: CHELLI

text: Because Diwali doesn't follow the sun. … It follows the moon.
speaker: ANNA

text: Your birthday follows the sun calendar, so it's the same date every year. But most of our festivals follow the moon.
speaker: ANNA

text: From one new moon to the next is about 29 and a half days. Twelve of those make only about 354 days.
speaker: ANNA

text: That's eleven days short!
speaker: CHELLI

text: Exactly. So every year, Diwali comes about eleven days earlier.
speaker: ANNA

text: Then why doesn't it end up in summer one day?
speaker: CHELLI

text: Because every two or three years, the calendar adds one extra month. It's called adhik maas. That pulls the festivals back into place.
speaker: ANNA

text: It's like a watch that runs a little fast. … Every few years, you fix the time.
speaker: ANNA

text: That's why Diwali always lands between mid-October and mid-November.
speaker: ANNA

text: You can see the difference with two festivals you know. Sankranti follows the sun, so it's almost always January 14th or 15th.
speaker: ANNA

text: And Eid follows the moon with no extra month. So it keeps moving about eleven days every year, through every season.
speaker: ANNA

text: And why that one night?
speaker: CHELLI

text: Diwali is on Amavasya, the new-moon night of the month of Kartika. … The night with no moon at all.
speaker: ANNA

text: The darkest night of the month… is the one night every lamp really shows.
speaker: ANNA

text: So next year?
speaker: CHELLI

text: October 29th, 2027. … About ten days earlier. Just like the moon says.
speaker: ANNA

text: Question two! Why do we clean the entire house before Diwali? Every single year.
speaker: CHELLI

text: Think about what just ended. … The monsoon.
speaker: ANNA

text: Four months of rain. Damp walls, fungus in the corners, that smell in the cupboards, insects everywhere.
speaker: ANNA

text: By Diwali, the rain stops and the air turns dry. It's the first good time in months to clean, dry, and paint.
speaker: ANNA

text: In our grandparents' time, homes had mud floors and lime-washed walls. Lime is a natural disinfectant, so after the rains, they washed the walls white again to fight the fungus.
speaker: ANNA

text: Today we have paint and tiles… but the habit stayed. Our ancestors built it around how they lived, and we still follow it, because the timing still makes sense.
speaker: ANNA

text: Shops do the same with money. … The old account books close, and new ones begin.
speaker: ANNA

text: So the cleaning isn't just tradition…
speaker: CHELLI

text: It's good timing. … And honestly, it's the only week the whole family cleans together.
speaker: ANNA

text: Question three! My friend says her Diwali bonus is a gift from her company. Is it?
speaker: CHELLI

text: For a lot of people, it's not a gift. … It's the law.
speaker: ANNA

text: India has a law from 1965, called the Payment of Bonus Act.
speaker: ANNA

text: If you earn up to 21,000 rupees a month… you've worked at least 30 days in the year… and your company has 20 or more people…
speaker: ANNA

text: …then the company must pay you a bonus. At least 8.33 percent, and up to 20 percent.
speaker: ANNA
